problem: Consider the matrix given by $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ k-3\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(B).$
worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(B),$ then the equation $Bx=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[B\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 7 & k-3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 5 & 7 & k-3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & k+2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & k-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ {x}_{2}=-1 \\ 0=k-1.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k-1,$ which means that $k=1.$
